predecessors.name: Northern Yuan
predecessors.text: the Oirat lands of western Mongolia (Hovd, Uvs, Bayan-Olgii, Dzavhan, Tuva and the Mongolian Altai)

successors.name: Mongol Khanate
successors.text: the Oirat homeland west of the Altai and Dzungaria, which the Eastern Mongols under Mandukhai and Dayan Khan 'pushed ... westward' from 1480

ledger.x: 1422: the Oirats hold the lands east of Lake Balkhash.
1434: Arughtai dies and the Oirats rule the Mongols.
1445: Esen forces Hami and Shazhou to accept Mongol titles.
1455: Hami is lost with Esen's fall.
1455: Esen is killed and the empire breaks up.
1480: the Eastern Mongols push the Oirats west.

wars.name: Oirat-Northern Yuan wars (Toghon against Arughtai and Adai Khan)
wars.outcome: Toghon pushes Arughtai east of the Khingan in 1433, kills him in 1434, installs Taisun as puppet khan and by 1437 has 'totally defeated Arugtai and ...

wars.name: Oirat wars with Uwais Khan of Moghulistan
wars.outcome: Uwais Khan is 'usually defeated and even captured twice' by the Oirats; the Oirats hold the Balkhash-Dzungaria lands.

wars.name: Esen Taishi's campaigns in Hami and against the Uriankhai guards
wars.outcome: Hami is attacked in 1443 and 1445 and Shazhou and Qizhin accept Mongol titles; the Daning and Duoyan guards are conquered by 1447; in winter 1450 Esen and Taisun raid the Jurchens into Heilongjiang.

wars.name: Tumu Crisis
wars.outcome: Esen invades in July 1449, destroys the Ming army at Yanghe (3 August), captures Emperor Yingzong (1 September), besieges Beijing briefly (27-30 August) and returns the emperor in September 1450; no frontier moves.

wars.name: Fall of Esen Taishi
wars.outcome: After Esen proclaims himself khan in 1453 Alag rebels and Esen is defeated and killed by Bukun (1455 in the infobox); 'Esen's death broke up the unity of the Oirats'.

wars.name: Mongol recovery of Mongolia from the Oirats
wars.outcome: From 1480 Mandukhai and Dayan Khan push the Oirats west; by 1510 Dayan Khan has unified the Mongol tribes including the Oirats and defeats the southwestern Mongols with the help of the Four Oirats.

certainty.note: A nomadic confederation without surveyed frontiers: the pages name regions (Hami and Turfan to Gansu, the Uriankhai lands, the Korean border) and peoples, never lines.
